chunks: Al-‘Ays ibn al-Qasim asked Aba ‘Abdillah عليه السلام about ghusl (ritual bath) at al-Mu‘arras.
So he said: “There is no ghusl required of you in it, and ta‘rīs is that one prays in it and lies down in it, whether one passes by it at night or by day.”

key_terms.التَّعْرِيسُ: staying briefly at a resting place by praying and lying down there
key_terms.الْمُعَرَّسِ: al-Mu‘arras, the resting place being referred to
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ: there is no obligation upon you

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required at al-Mu‘arras, and what does ta‘rīs mean there?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding al-Mu‘arras, stating that ghusl is not required there. It also defines ta‘rīs as praying and lying down at that place, whether during the night or the day.
